title: IMURAN (azathioprine) 50 mg scored tablets: full prescribing information
authors: US Food and Drug Administration (labelling submitted by Legacy Pharma USA Inc.)
journal: US Food and Drug Administration approved prescribing information, via DailyMed; version 1, effective 19 March 2026
funder: not stated; FDA-approved labelling carries no funding statement
result: Azathioprine is cleaved to 6-mercaptopurine, which hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase and kinases convert to 6-thioguanine nucleotides; cytotoxicity follows in part from their incorporation into DNA. Mercaptopurine has two major inactivation routes: thiol methylation, catalysed by thiopurine S-methyltransferase (TPMT), to methyl-6-mercaptopurine, and oxidation, catalysed by xanthine oxidase, to 6-thiouric acid; NUDT15 converts 6-thioguanine nucleotides to inactive monophosphates. TPMT activity correlates inversely with 6-thioguanine nucleotide concentrations in erythrocytes, which have negligible xanthine oxidase activity. About 0.3%, or 1 in 300, of patients of European or African ancestry carry two loss-of-function TPMT alleles and have little or no TPMT activity, and about 10% carry one, giving intermediate activity. Patients with reduced TPMT or NUDT15 activity given usual doses accumulate 6-thioguanine nucleotides and are at higher risk of severe myelosuppression, and those with TPMT or NUDT15 deficiency require alternative therapy or dose modification.
